doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Work permit limits and the Royal Academy of Music
summary: Having to leave England every three months stopped Carter from starting formal study at the Academy.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You mentioned the problems you had because of the work permit problem, which we won’t get into, the reciprocity between the British union and the U.S. unions, and the reason for which you couldn’t play, actually. You had to leave the country every three months.
Yeah, to get a reentry permit. We’re going to wind up with more than six hours, though. I think we’ll have to.
Otherwise, we’re into the . . . where are we now?
Well, okay. Can you stay until next Saturday?
At this rate, I may have to stay until your next birthday.

Moving along, however, I know we had discussed your education, you know, various self-education, teachers, and everything, and I know in England you had an aspiration of actually undertaking some formal study, which was sort of made impossible by this constant leaving the country. But could you tell us what that involved?

Yes. I had intended undergoing some studies there. As a matter of fact, I went to the Royal Academy of Music, and had an interview with a professor . . . what was his name? Oh, boy. I had it on the tip of my tongue, and now it escapes me. But anyway, the problem was that I had to leave the country every three months and reapply for an entry permit, and I just couldn’t start any course of study that would be interrupted. He felt that it wouldn’t work too well. So I just put it off, and I resumed many years later after I got to Hollywood
And we will get to that, of course, eventually. [laughs] Maybe in about six weeks at this rate.
